evidence.claim: 4 of 5 reviewers re-key certificate values from the PDF into a spreadsheet before comparing them with the specification
The median review takes 11 minutes per lot (n = 40); re-keying is about 6 of them
3 of 4 out-of-spec lots were missed on first review (37 of 40 lots correct first time)
Reviewers want each value next to its limit before deciding
evidence.quote: I need to see the number next to the limit, not scroll between them

evidence.claim: The SOP requires a written rationale for every hold or reject, attributable to a named reviewer with a time
Unreadable values are escalated by phone to the QA lead, with no record
evidence.quote: I only hear about unreadable certificates when someone calls me

evidence.claim: In the paper test, 4 of 5 reviewers released a compliant lot from the derived verdict without re-keying
Supplier notices are drafted by the reviewer and sent by the supplier-quality manager
The QA lead agreed the lot-release flow and that the tool never releases a lot itself
Plant tablets have no internet access; tools must run offline

insights.statement: Re-keying is both the time sink and the error source
Reviewers trust a derived verdict when they can see the value next to its limit
Escalations for unreadable values are invisible today
Every decision must be attributable and explained; sending stays with supplier quality

assumptions.statement: Reviewers will release from a derived verdict without re-keying values
Showing the derivation next to each result is enough to catch a misread
The supplier-quality manager will reuse the reviewer's notice draft
Sixteen lots represent a realistic shift queue

open_questions.question: Can the plant's LIMS export certificate values as structured data?
open_questions.trigger: The LIMS owner confirms the export format

missing: Structured certificate exports from the LIMS (none provided)
